encounter.clinical_summary: John Carter, a 58-year-old male with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia, presented to the emergency department with intermittent substernal chest pressure lasting approximately two hours. Initial electrocardiogram findings showed no acute ST-segment elevation. Serial troponin measurements remained within the normal reference range. The patient received aspirin and was placed under observation overnight. No evidence of acute coronary syndrome was identified, and outpatient cardiology follow-up was recommended.
